q42.q: GLP-1 receptor agonists and weight loss in non-diabetic adults
q42.rewrite: GLP-1 receptor agonists and weight loss in adults without diabetes
q42.hyde:
Title: Weight loss with GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults without diabetes: a review of the evidence

Abstract: GLP-1 receptor agonists are medicines that copy a natural hormone called GLP-1, which helps control hunger and how much food the body stores. These medicines are widely used to treat type 2 diabetes, but some adults without diabetes also use them to lose weight. We reviewed the research on how much weight these medicines help people without diabetes lose. We found that they can produce weight loss, but the amount varies from person to person. The medicines also have side effects, such as nausea and vomiting, and they can cause problems with blood sugar control. Our review shows that these medicines can be useful for weight loss in people without diabetes, but they should be used
q42.title: Weight Loss With GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Adults Without Diabetes: A Review of the Evidence

q43.q: graph neural networks for molecular property prediction
q43.rewrite: graph neural networks for predicting molecular properties
q43.hyde:
Predicting Molecular Properties with Graph Neural Networks: A Review of Methods and Applications

Graph neural networks are computer models that learn from data arranged as networks, where each item is a point and the links between items are edges. Molecules are naturally described this way: atoms are the points, and the chemical bonds between them are the edges. This paper reviews how researchers use graph neural networks to predict molecular properties, such as how a substance behaves or how it reacts with other substances. We describe the main methods, the kinds of problems they tackle, and how well they perform. We also discuss the challenges they face and point to directions for future research. Our aim is to give a clear overview of this area for researchers who want to understand or use these models.
q43.title: Predicting Molecular Properties with Graph Neural Networks: A Review of Methods and Applications

q44.q: ocean acidification effects on coral calcification
q44.rewrite: How ocean acidification affects coral calcification
q44.hyde:
How Ocean Acidification Affects the Way Corals Build Their Skeletons

Abstract

As the ocean takes up carbon dioxide from the air, seawater becomes more acidic. This process, called ocean acidification, can make it harder for corals to build their skeletons from calcium carbonate, the same mineral found in chalk and seashells. In this study, we measured how acidification changes the rate at which corals lay down this mineral, a process called calcification. We used corals kept in tanks with carefully controlled water chemistry and compared their skeletons with those of corals in normal seawater. We found that more acidic water slowed down calcification, leaving the skeletons thinner and less dense. q45.q: long-term cognitive outcomes after COVID-19 infection
q45.rewrite: long-term effects of COVID-19 infection on thinking and memory
q45.hyde:
Long-Term Effects of COVID-19 Infection on Cognition: A Systematic Review of Studies Following People for Months or Years

We systematically reviewed studies that followed people for months or years after COVID-19 infection to find out how their thinking, memory, and attention changed over time. We searched for studies that measured these abilities, called cognition, and reported results at least several months after infection. We included studies of people of all ages and of people with or without COVID-19 symptoms. We then grouped the findings by the type of thinking skill measured and by how long after infection the measurements were taken. Our review brings together evidence from many studies to show which changes in cognition have been found, how large they were, and how long they lasted.
q45.title: Long-Term Effects of COVID-19 Infection on Cognition: A Review of Research Findings

q46.rewrite: Experiments that look for dark matter particles directly
q46.hyde:
Title: Direct Detection of Dark Matter: Experiments and What They Reveal

Abstract: Dark matter is a form of matter that does not give off or reflect light, so we cannot see it directly. Scientists think it makes up a large share of the matter in the universe. To find it, researchers run direct detection experiments, which look for the tiny signals that dark matter particles would make when they bump into ordinary atoms. In this paper, we explain how these experiments work and what they have found so far. We describe the different kinds of detectors, the challenges of picking out a real signal from background noise, and the latest results. We also discuss what these experiments mean for our understanding of the universe.
q46.title: Direct Detection of Dark Matter: Experiments and Their Results

q47.q: machine learning for early sepsis detection in intensive care
q47.rewrite: machine learning for early detection of sepsis in intensive care
q47.hyde:
Using Machine Learning to Spot Sepsis Early in Intensive Care

Abstract

Sepsis is a dangerous whole-body reaction to infection, and it can kill quickly. In intensive care, doctors need to recognize it early so they can act fast. In this study, we tested whether machine learning—computer programs that learn patterns from examples—can help doctors spot sepsis early. We used real patient records from an intensive care unit. We compared several machine learning methods to see how well each one could tell patients with sepsis apart from patients without it. We also checked how well each method worked for patients with different kinds of infections. Our results show that machine learning can help doctors recognize sepsis early. This could help patients get the care they need sooner.
q47.title: Using Machine Learning to Detect Sepsis Early in Intensive Care

q48.q: urban green space and mental health
q48.rewrite: urban green space and mental health
q48.hyde:
How Green Spaces in Cities Relate to People's Mental Health: A Review of the Research

Abstract

Green spaces in cities, such as parks and tree-lined streets, have been linked to people's mental health. In this review, we bring together research on how these spaces relate to mental health. We explain the main ways researchers have studied this question and what they have found. We also point out gaps in the research and suggest what future studies could do. Our aim is to help people understand the evidence and plan how to use green spaces to support mental health.

q49.q: CRISPR base editing for sickle cell disease
q49.rewrite: CRISPR base editing for sickle cell disease
q49.hyde:
CRISPR Base Editing for Sickle Cell Disease: A Review of Recent Research

Abstract

Sickle cell disease is a genetic illness in which red blood cells become misshapen and can damage the body. CRISPR base editing is a way to change a single DNA letter inside a cell without cutting the DNA strand. In this review, we bring together recent research on using base editing to treat sickle cell disease. We explain how the method works, what results studies have found so far, and what challenges remain. We also discuss how this approach compares with other ways of treating the disease. Our aim is to give a clear picture of the current state of this research.
q49.title: CRISPR Base Editing for Sickle Cell Disease: A Review of Recent Research and Future Directions

q50.rewrite: Detecting when language models produce false or misleading information
q50.hyde:
Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models: A Review of Methods for Spotting False Claims in AI-Generated Text

Large language models are computer programs that produce text, but they sometimes make up facts that sound convincing. These false claims are called hallucinations. In this review, we bring together the main ways researchers check for them. We explain how each method works, what it can and cannot do, and how well it performs. We also look at how these methods can be combined and what challenges remain. Our aim is to give a clear picture of the current tools for spotting false claims in AI-generated text.
q50.title: Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models: Methods, Challenges, and Future Directions

q51.hyde:
Vitamin D and Depression: A Review of the Evidence

Vitamin D is a nutrient that the body makes when sunlight reaches the skin, and it also comes from food and supplements. Depression is a common mental health condition that affects how people feel, think and act. In this review, we bring together research on whether vitamin D is linked to depression. We explain what the studies have found and what the evidence means for people's health. We use standard scientific terms and do not invent any numbers.
q51.title: Vitamin D and Depression: A Review of the Evidence on Their Link and Whether Vitamin D Can Help Treat Depression

q52.hyde:
How Turmeric's Active Compound Curcumin Reduces Inflammation: A Review of the Evidence

Inflammation is the body's response to injury or irritation, and it can cause swelling, pain and other problems when it lasts too long. Turmeric, a yellow spice, contains a substance called curcumin that may help reduce inflammation. In this review, we bring together research on how curcumin works and how well it reduces inflammation. We explain what the studies found and what the evidence means for using turmeric to help with inflammation.
q52.title: Turmeric and Inflammation: How Its Active Compound Curcumin Reduces Inflammation in the Body

q53.hyde:
Predicting the Price of Bitcoin: A Study of How Well Different Models Forecast Its Value

Abstract

We set out to find out how well different prediction methods can forecast the price of Bitcoin, a digital currency that is traded on many markets. We compared several models, which are mathematical tools that learn patterns from past data, and tested how accurately each one predicted future prices. We also looked at how the models performed when they were given different amounts of information about the market. Our results show that some models predict prices better than others, and that the amount of information they receive makes a difference to how accurate their forecasts are. These findings help people understand what makes predicting Bitcoin prices difficult and which methods work best.
q53.title: Predicting the Price of Bitcoin: A Study of Forecasting Methods and Their Accuracy

q54.rewrite: How stable are perovskite solar cells?
q54.hyde:
How to Make Perovskite Solar Cells Last Longer: Improving Their Stability

Abstract

Perovskite solar cells are a promising kind of solar panel, but they tend to break down over time. In this paper, we explain what makes them unstable and how to make them last longer. We first describe the main ways these cells fail, such as damage from moisture, heat, and light. We then explain the methods researchers use to protect them, including adding protective layers and changing the materials inside the cell. We also discuss how to test whether a cell stays stable over time. Our aim is to give a clear picture of the problems and the solutions, so that people can better understand how to make these solar cells more reliable.
q54.title: How Long Do Perovskite Solar Cells Last? Improving Their Stability for Real-World Use

q55.hyde:
The Riemann Hypothesis: A New Approach to Proving It

The Riemann hypothesis is one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. It concerns the Riemann zeta function, a mathematical function that connects the pattern of prime numbers to the values of a function. The hypothesis makes a claim about where the function's zeros lie. In this paper, we offer a new approach to proving it. We begin by explaining the basic ideas behind the hypothesis and the tools we use. We then present our main result: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. We finish by discussing what this result means for mathematics and for the study of prime numbers.
q55.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: A Century of Progress Toward Proving That All Non-Trivial Zeros of the Zeta Function Lie on the Critical Line

q56.hyde:
The Roman Economy: How Trade, Money, and Taxation Shaped the Roman Empire

Abstract

This paper examines how the Roman economy worked, focusing on trade, money, and taxation. We explore how these systems supported the Roman Empire and how they changed over time. We also consider how the economy affected daily life and the wider society of the Roman world. By bringing together evidence from different sources, we aim to give a clear picture of the Roman economy and its lasting importance.
q56.title: How the Roman Empire's Economy Worked: Trade, Money, and the Spread of Roman Power

q58.hyde:
Does Yoga Help With Back Pain? A Review of the Research

Yoga may help people with back pain, but the research so far has not given a clear answer. In this review, we bring together studies that tested whether yoga helps people with back pain. We explain what each study found and what the results mean for people who have back pain. We also point out what is still unknown. Our aim is to help people understand the evidence and make informed choices about using yoga for back pain.
q58.title: Does Yoga Help with Back Pain? A Review of the Research

How Meditation Changes the Body's Stress Response: A Review of Research

Meditation changes how the body responds to stress. In this review, we bring together research on how meditation affects the body's stress response. We explain the main ways meditation can help people cope with stress. We also describe the different kinds of meditation and the different ways researchers measure stress. Finally, we look at what the research shows about how meditation affects the body's stress response.

q60.hyde:
Essential Oils: A Review of Their Chemical Makeup and Effects on Health

Essential oils are concentrated mixtures of natural chemicals that give plants their smell. In this review, we bring together what is known about which chemicals these oils contain and how they affect health. We explain how the oils are made and how they are used, and we look at the evidence for their effects on the body. We also discuss the gaps in what we know and what future research should explore.
